description: A group of computer engineering students from Technological Institute of the Philippines Quezon City, ready to assemble!
summary:
ARES-V is an interactive 3D orbital-to-surface exploration and spacesuit HUD built to help future Mars astronauts conduct safe, high-value geological EVAs. Starting from a 380 km orbital view powered by NASA Mars Trek, MOLA topography, Odyssey THEMIS thermal inertia, and MRO SHARAD subsurface ice layers, crews deploy directly onto four historic NASA rover corridors: Jezero Crater (Perseverance), Mount Sharp's 2025 boxwork formations in Gale Crater (Curiosity), Meridiani Planum (Opportunity), and Gusev Crater (Spirit).

On the surface, ARES-V layers optical imagery, HiRISE slope-hazard masks, USGS geologic units, and Curiosity RAD radiation telemetry onto a first-person visor and Field Slate with slope-aware safe-route pathfinding. Because astronaut safety comes first, the system simulates real-time O₂, suit thermal reserves, stamina, and 25 kg sample mass strain, delivering live safety advisories, lander airlock resupply, and an unlockable planetary geology archive.
details:
ARES-V (Augmented Reconnaissance & EVA System) is a 3D orbital-to-surface Mars exploration and spacesuit navigation interface designed around a continuous two-stage mission loop:

  1. Orbital Reconnaissance: Users inspect a 3D Mars globe layered with Optical (NASA JPL Mars Trek / MRO MARCI), Thermal (Mars Odyssey THEMIS thermal inertia), and Subsurface Ice (MRO SHARAD radar) datasets. Selecting one of four historic NASA landing sites (Jezero Crater, Mount Sharp in Gale Crater, Meridiani Planum, or Gusev Crater) triggers a smooth orbital plunge dive to the surface.
  2. First-Person Surface EVA & Field Slate: On the ground, the astronaut uses a diegetic visor HUD and wrist-mounted Field Slate (M) to toggle between Optical, Topo / Obstacles (HiRISE DEM contours and slope/boulder hazard masks), USGS Geology (mudstone, sulfate veins, and Curiosity's 2025 boxwork formations), and Rad / Weather (Curiosity RAD ionizing radiation and dust opacity).
  3. Safe-Traverse Pathfinding & Sample Return: A slope-aware pathfinder computes safe walking routes around steep scarps and boulder traps. Astronauts scan and core 24 priority geological specimens (6 per site), inspect Sol 0 touchdown monuments and NASA rovers to unlock a Sites & Rovers heritage archive, and return to the lander airlock to vault samples and replenish suit reserves. Completing all sites unlocks a Global Expedition Report and a downloadable Planetary Field Geologist Certificate.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Astronaut Safety First: Real-time physiological modeling tracks suit O₂, thermal/heater reserves, stamina, heart rate, and 25 kg core pack mass strain. A live Suit Status & Safety Advisory bar warns crew members early when to rest on steep terrain, offload heavy cores, or return to the lander before reserves reach critical levels.
  • Actionable Multi-Layer Context: Instead of forcing astronauts to read disconnected charts, ARES-V fuses orbital and surface datasets directly into their visor and Field Slate so science goals and terrain hazards are evaluated together in real time.
  • Public Science & STEM Outreach: Beyond mission operations prototyping, ARES-V lets students and researchers walk real NASA rover corridors (Perseverance, Curiosity, Opportunity, and Spirit) and understand why each crater and core sample matters for Mars's habitability history.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used

  • Languages & Core Stack: JavaScript (ES6+), React 18, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS 4, Zustand 5
  • 3D Graphics & Custom Shaders: Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber), @react-three/drei, custom GLSL shaders for atmospheric scattering and multi-layer orbital/surface overlays, and procedural vertex-displaced rock geometry
  • Audio & Export: Web Audio API (zero-asset synthesized suit breathing, heartbeat, spectrometer scan hum, radio squelch, and thruster audio) and HTML5 Canvas API for high-resolution PNG certificate generation
  • Data Sources: NASA JPL Mars Trek WMTS, MGS MOLA, Mars Odyssey THEMIS, MRO HiRISE / SHARAD, Mars 2020 & MSL MMGIS traverse data, Curiosity RAD, and USGS Astrogeology

Creativity and Key Factors Considered

  • Seamless Orbit-to-Surface Continuity: Rather than abrupt screen cuts, ARES-V animates atmospheric plunge dives, orbital ascents, and suborbital site-to-site transfers across the 3D globe.
  • Load vs. Survival Tradeoff: Carrying more rock cores increases pack mass (25 kg cap), accelerates oxygen burn, and drains stamina faster on >15° slopes, creating realistic EVA planning decisions.
  • Zero-Clutter Diegetic UX: Controls, route plotting, mineral spectra, and historical rover archives live inside the astronaut's Field Slate and minimal visor reticles, so the Martian terrain remains the focus.
